   241	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   242	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   243	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   244	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   245	  toFun x := fun k =>
   246	    match k with
   247	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   248	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   249	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   250	  map_add' x y := by
   251	    funext k
   252	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   253	    · simp
   254	    · simp
   255	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   256	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   257	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   258	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   259	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   261	        rfl
   262	  map_smul' c x := by
   263	    funext k
   264	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   265	    · simp
   266	    · simp
   267	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   268	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   269	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   270	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   271	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   272	        rfl

   392	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :

   394	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   395	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩

   399	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   400	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   401	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   402	  have hval :
   403	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   404	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +

    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,

    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is

   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.

   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.

   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.

   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}

   753	/-- A partition of the ambient coordinates identifies ambient vectors with
   754	tuples of vectors on the partition registers. -/
   755	private noncomputable def coordinatePartitionEquiv {K ι J : Type*}
   756	    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   757	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   758	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) : (ι → K) ≃ ∀ j, V j → K where
   759	  toFun x := fun _ a => x a
   760	  invFun x := ∑ j, extendRegister (V j) (x j)
   761	  left_inv x := by
   762	    funext a
   763	    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   764	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (fun b => x b)) a = x a
   765	    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   766	    · simp [extendRegister, haj]
   767	    · intro i _ hij
   768	      have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   769	        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   770	      simp [extendRegister, hai]
   771	    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   772	  right_inv x := by
   773	    funext j a
   774	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (x i)) a.1 = x j a
   775	    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   776	    · simp [extendRegister, a.2]
   777	    · intro i _ hij
   778	      have hai : a.1 ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   779	        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai a.2
   780	      simp [extendRegister, hai]
   781	    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim

   426	/-- The sum of the first linear pieces of a finite family of positive-level
   427	conditionally-linear terms. -/
   428	private def condLinearHeadSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   429	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] {ell : ℕ}
   430	    (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) :
   431	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   432	  toFun x := ∑ j, (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (t j).headSupport x)
   433	  map_add' x y := by
   434	    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   435	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   436	    intro j _
   437	    rw [← map_add]
   438	    congr 1
   439	    ext b
   440	    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]
   441	  map_smul' c x := by
   442	    rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   443	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   444	    intro j _
   445	    rw [← map_smul]
   446	    congr 1
   447	    ext b
   448	    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]

   450	/-- Combine equal-level representations of conditionally linear functions on
   451	disjoint registers. -/
   452	private def CondLinearTerm.directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   453	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   454	    (V : J → Finset ι) :
   455	    (ell : ℕ) → (J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) →
   456	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   457	  | 0, _ => .zero
   458	  | ell + 1, t =>
   459	      .succ (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) (condLinearHeadSum t)
   460	        (by
   461	          intro x a ha
   462	          simp only [condLinearHeadSum, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
   463	            Finset.sum_apply]
   464	          apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   465	          intro j _
   466	          exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   467	            (fun haj => ha (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)))
   468	        (fun y => directSum (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   469	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y)))

   471	private theorem CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   472	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   473	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   474	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   475	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) :
   476	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t)
   477	      (Finset.univ.biUnion V) := by
   478	  induction ell generalizing V with
   479	  | zero => trivial
   480	  | succ ell ih =>
   481	      have hhead (j : J) : (t j).headSupport ⊆ V j :=
   482	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   483	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   484	      · exact Finset.biUnion_subset.mpr fun j _ =>
   485	          (hhead j).trans (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem V (Finset.mem_univ j))
   486	      · intro y
   487	        have htail (j : J) :
   488	            CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   489	              ((t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y))
   490	              (V j \ (t j).headSupport) :=
   491	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) _
   492	        have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   493	            Disjoint (V i \ (t i).headSupport) (V j \ (t j).headSupport) := by
   494	          intro i j hij
   495	          exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   496	        have hrec := ih _ hDisjointTail _ htail
   497	        have hunion :
   498	            Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) =
   499	              Finset.univ.biUnion V \
   500	                Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => (t j).headSupport) := by
   501	          ext a
   502	          constructor
   503	          · intro ha
   504	            obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp ha
   505	            obtain ⟨haV, haS⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hj
   506	            refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr
   507	              ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haV⟩, ?_⟩
   508	            intro haHeads
   509	            obtain ⟨i, _, hai⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp haHeads
   510	            by_cases hij : i = j
   511	            · subst i
   512	              exact haS hai
   513	            · exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) (hhead i hai) haV
   514	          · intro ha
   515	            obtain ⟨j, _, haV⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1
   516	            refine Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
   517	              ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨haV, ?_⟩⟩
   518	            intro haj
   519	            exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).2
   520	              (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)
   521	        simpa only [hunion] using hrec

   523	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   524	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   525	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   526	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   527	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) (x : ι → K) :
   528	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t) x =
   529	      ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   530	  induction ell generalizing V x with
   531	  | zero =>
   532	      apply Eq.symm
   533	      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   534	      intro j _
   535	      cases t j
   536	      rfl
   537	  | succ ell ih =>
   538	      let S : J → Finset ι := fun j => (t j).headSupport
   539	      let y : J → ι → K := fun j =>
   540	        (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   541	      have hS (j : J) : S j ⊆ V j :=
   542	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   543	      have hy (j : J) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) : y j a = 0 := by
   544	        exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   545	          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
   546	      have hhead :
   547	          condLinearHeadSum t
   548	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
   549	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   550	        intro j _
   551	        change (t j).headLinear
   552	            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
   553	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
   554	          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   555	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
   556	          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
   557	      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
   558	        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
   559	      have htail (j : J) :
   560	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   561	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   562	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   563	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   564	        intro i j hij
   565	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   566	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   567	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   568	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   569	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   570	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   571	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   572	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   573	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   574	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   575	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   576	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   577	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
   578	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
   579	        change (t j).headLinear
   580	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   581	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   582	              ((t j).tail
   583	                ((t j).headLinear
   584	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   585	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   586	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
   587	        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   588	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   589	        rw [htail_eval]
   590	      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
   591	        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
   592	      have htail_family :
   593	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   594	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   595	        funext j
   596	        rw [hselect]
   597	      calc
   598	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   599	            (∑ j, y j) +
   600	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   601	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   602	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
   603	              change condLinearHeadSum t
   604	                    (coordinateRestriction
   605	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   606	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   607	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   608	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   609	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   610	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   611	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   612	                            (coordinateRestriction
   613	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   614	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   615	              rw [htail_family]
   616	        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   617	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   618	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   619	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   620	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   621	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   622	              intro j _
   623	              exact (hcomponent j).symm

   625	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   626	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   627	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   628	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   629	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   630	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   631	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   632	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   633	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   634	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   635	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   636	  classical
   637	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   638	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   639	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   640	  funext x
   641	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   642	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   643	  intro j _
   644	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   645	
   646	/--
   647	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   648	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   649	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   650	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.

   652	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   653	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   654	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   655	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   656	
   657	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   658	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   659	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   660	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   661	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   662	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   663	-/
   664	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   665	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   666	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   667	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   668	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   669	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   670	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   671	
   672	/--
   673	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   674	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:548-559`, with
   675	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   676	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   677	-/
   678	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   679	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   680	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   681	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   682	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   683	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   684	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   685	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   686	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   687	  classical
   688	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   689	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   690	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   691	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   692	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   693	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   694	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   695	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   696	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   697	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   698	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   699	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   700	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   701	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   702	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   703	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   704	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   705	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   706	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   707	    have huniv :
   708	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   709	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   710	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   711	      ext i
   712	      cases i <;> simp
   713	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   714	  · funext x
   715	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   716	    simp only [zero_add]
   717	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   718	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   719	    rfl

   721	/--
   722	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   723	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   724	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:679-691`;

   726	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   727	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.

   729	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   730	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   731	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   732	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   733	
   734	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   735	nonempty.  This is `lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   736	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:693-698`. -/
   737	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   738	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   739	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   740	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   741	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   742	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   743	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   744	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   745

     4

     6	the behavior of such maps and their shared-seed distributions under finite
     7	coordinate direct sums.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source results are `lem:cl-kth`, `lem:cl-func-prod`, and
    12	`lem:cl-dist-prod` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-587`, with
    13	paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-379`.

    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- The value of the strict-prefix marginal preceding `k`. This is a
    24	formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-kth`, blueprint
    25	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`, paper
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
    27	def clPrefix {K ι : Type*} [Zero K] {ell : ℕ}
    28	    (marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (k : Fin ell)
    29	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    30	  if _hk : k.val = 0 then 0
    31	  else marginal ⟨k.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) k.isLt⟩ x
    32	
    33	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
    34	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
    35	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`, paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
    37	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    38	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
    39	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
    40	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    41	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
    42	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
    43	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/

     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:433-492`.
    14	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    22	
    23	/--
    24	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    25	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`;
    26	paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    28	-/
    29	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    30	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    31	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    32	
    33	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    34	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    36	-/
    37	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    38	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    39	  Pi.single i 1
    40	
    41	/--
    42	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    43	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    45	-/
    46	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    47	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    48	
    49	/--
    50	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    51	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`; paper origin
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    53	-/
    54	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    55	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    56	
    57	/--
    58	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    59	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:455-466`,
    60	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    61	-/
    62	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    63	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    64	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    65	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := h
    66	  ext x
    67	  constructor
    68	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    69	    exact ⟨s - t, by module⟩
    70	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    71	    exact ⟨t + s, by module⟩
    72	
    73	/--
    74	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    75	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    76	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    79	-/
    80	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    81	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    82	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))
    83	
    84	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the
    85	canonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/
    86	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint
    87	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
    88	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`.
    89	-/
    90	noncomputable def lineRep {m : ℕ}
    91	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
    92	  lineRepMap v u
    93	
    94	/--
    95	Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:line-representative`
    96	(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`).
    98	The canonical representative map is a projection whose kernel is the line
    99	`K v`, so a point and its canonical representative differ by a scalar multiple
   100	of the direction.
   101	-/
   102	theorem sub_lineRepMap_mem_span {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
   103	    u - lineRepMap v u ∈ Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)) := by
   104	  have hc :
   105	      IsCompl
   106	        (registerSubmodule K
   107	          (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))))
   108	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) :=
   109	    (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement
   110	      (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))).symm
   111	  have hrep : lineRepMap v u =
   112	      (registerSubmodule K
   113	        (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))))).projection
   114	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) hc u := rfl
   115	  rw [hrep, ← Submodule.projection_eq_self_sub_projection hc u]
   116	  exact Submodule.projection_apply_mem hc.symm u
   117	
   118	/--
   119	Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:line-representative`
   120	(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
   121	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`).
   122	Every point lies on the line through its own canonical representative in the
   123	same direction; this is the incidence property used by the line-versus-point
   124	samplers.
   125	-/
   126	theorem mem_linePoints_lineRepMap {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
   127	    u ∈ linePoints (lineRepMap v u) v := by
   128	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v u)
   129	  exact ⟨t, by rw [ht]; abel⟩

496	Thus, for a fixed direction, a line is an equivalence class of its points: the
   497	pair $(u,v)$ representing it can use any base point on the line. A canonical
   498	representation is obtained as follows.
   499	
   500	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]\label{def:line-representative}
   501		\uses{def:line, def:cl-canonical, prop:line-equiv}
   502		Let $\ell$ be a line in direction $v \neq 0$, and let
   503		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   504		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$
   505		(Definition~\ref{def:cl-canonical}). The \emph{canonical representative of
   506		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   507		\[
   508			u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u) \qquad \text{for all } u \in \ell\;.
   509		\]
   510		This is well defined: since the image and kernel of $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ are
   511		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   512		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and
   513		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u_0) = u_0$; moreover any two points of $\ell$ differ by
   514		a multiple of $v$ and therefore have the same image under
   515		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$. A line $\ell = \ell(u,v)$ is henceforth canonically
   516		represented by the pair $(u_0, v)$. (For $v = 0$, where the singleton
   517		$\{u\}$ leaves no independent kernel basis, we take $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_0$ to
   518		be the identity---the canonical linear map with empty kernel basis---so
   519		that $u_0 = u$; the source leaves this case implicit.)
   520	\end{definition}

   522	\section{Quantum registers and EPR states}
   523	% Paper label sec:lin-reg kept for cross-reference fidelity.
   524	\label{sec:lin-reg}
   525	
   526	\begin{definition}[State space of a linear register]\label{def:lin-reg}
   527		\uses{def:complementary}
   528		For a set $V$, we write $\C^V$ for the complex vector space of dimension
   529		$|V|$, endowed with the canonical orthonormal basis
   530		$\{\ket{x}\}_{x \in V}$. A \emph{quantum state on $V$} is a unit vector

   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩

   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the

   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=

   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary

   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   153	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j

   524	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`

   529	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=

   534	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   535	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   536	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   537	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   539	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   540	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   541	  toFun
   542	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   543	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   544	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   545	  invFun
   546	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   547	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   548	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   549	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   550	  right_inv := by
   551	    intro x
   552	    cases x with
   553	    | inl a => rfl
   554	    | inr x =>
   555	        cases x with
   556	        | inl a => rfl
   557	        | inr a => rfl

   565	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   566	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   567	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   568	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   569	-/
   570	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   571	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   572	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   573	
   574	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   575	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   576	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   577	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   578	-/
   579	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   580	  match t, a with
   581	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   582	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   583	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   584	  | _, _ => false
   585	
   586	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   587	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   588	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   589	-/
   590	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   591	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   592	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   593	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   594	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   595	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   596	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   597	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   598	
   599	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   600	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   601	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   602	-/
   603	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   604	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   605	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   606	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   607	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   608	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   609	
   610	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   611	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   612	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   613	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   614	-/
   615	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   616	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   617	  open Classical in
   618	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   619	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   620	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   621	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   622	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   623	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   624	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   625	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   626	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   627	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   628	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   629	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   630	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   631	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   632	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   633	      else false
   634	
   635	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   636	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   637	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   638	-/
   639	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   640	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   641	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   642	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   643	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   644	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   645	  μ_prob := by
   646	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   647	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)) _
   648	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   649	
   650	end

   198	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :

   200	  toFun x := fun i =>
   201	    match i with
   202	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0

   204	    | .inr _ => 0

   212	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   213	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every

   215	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   216	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   217	  toFun x := fun i =>
   218	    match i with
   219	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   220	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   221	    | .inr _ => 0
   222	  map_add' x y := by
   223	    funext i
   224	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   225	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   226	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   227	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   228	      rfl
   229	    · simp
   230	    · simp
   231	  map_smul' c x := by
   232	    funext i
   233	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   234	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   235	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   236	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   237	      rfl
   238	    · simp
   239	    · simp

   243	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :

   257	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   258	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val

   289	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldPointRegister P →
   290	      ldPointCLLinear P v x i = 0 := by
   291	  intro x i hi
   292	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   293	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hi
   294	  · rfl
   295	  · rfl

   297	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the prefix-zeroing map vanishes
   298	outside the direction register. -/
   299	private theorem ldDirectionCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   300	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (k : LdIndex P), k ∉ ldDirectionRegister P →
   301	      ldDirectionCLLinear P i x k = 0 := by
   302	  intro x k hk
   303	  rcases k with (j | u) | j
   304	  · rfl
   305	  · rfl
   306	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hk
   307	
   308	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   309	the scalar register. -/
   310	private theorem ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   311	    ldPointRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   312	  intro i hi
   313	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   314	  simp [ldSeedRegister]
   315	
   316	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the direction register is disjoint
   317	from the scalar register. -/
   318	private theorem ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed (P : LdParams) :
   319	    ldDirectionRegister P ⊆ Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P := by
   320	  intro i hi
   321	  obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   322	  simp [ldSeedRegister]

   324	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point register is disjoint from
   325	both the scalar and the direction registers. -/

   327	    ldPointRegister P ⊆
   328	      (Finset.univ \ ldSeedRegister P) \ ldDirectionRegister P := by
   329	  intro i hi

   333	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the scalar register
   334	leaves the shared scalar coordinate unchanged. -/
   335	private theorem coordinateRestriction_seed (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   336	    coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) =
   337	      x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) := by
   338	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldSeedRegister P :=
   339	    Finset.mem_singleton_self _
   340	  simp [coordinateRestriction, hmem]

   342	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the point register
   343	leaves the point block unchanged. -/
   344	private theorem coordinateRestriction_point (P : LdParams) (x : LdSpace P) :
   345	    LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) = LdSpace.point x := by
   346	  funext j
   347	  have hmem : (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P) ∈ ldPointRegister P :=
   348	    Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)
   349	  simp [LdSpace.point, coordinateRestriction, hmem]

   351	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: restricting to the direction register
   352	leaves the direction block unchanged. -/

   354	    LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) =
   355	      LdSpace.direction x := by

   358	    Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)

   361	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the two-level conditionally linear syntax
   362	term realizing `ldALineCL`. -/
   363	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   364	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   365	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   366	    fun y =>
   367	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   368	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   369	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   370	        fun _ => .zero

   372	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the three-level conditionally linear syntax
   373	term realizing `ldDLineCL`. -/
   374	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   375	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   376	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   377	    fun y =>
   378	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   379	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))
   380	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   381	        fun w =>
   382	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   383	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   384	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   385	            fun _ => .zero
   386	
   387	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   388	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   389	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   390	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   391	-/
   392	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   393	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   394	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   395	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   396	  funext x
   397	  have hseed :
   398	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   399	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   400	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   401	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   402	  have hval :
   403	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   404	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   405	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   406	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   407	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   408	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   409	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   410	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   411	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   412	    rw [hseed]
   413	  rw [hval]
   414	  funext i
   415	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   416	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   417	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   418	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   419	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   420	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   421	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   422	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   423	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   424	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   425	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   426	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   427	
   428	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   429	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   430	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   431	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   432	-/
   433	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   434	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   435	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   436	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   437	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   438	  funext x
   439	  have hseed :
   440	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   441	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   442	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   443	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   444	  have hdir :
   445	      LdSpace.direction
   446	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   447	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) =
   448	        prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by
   449	    funext j
   450	    change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   451	        (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
   452	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]
   453	  have hval :
   454	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
   455	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   456	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   457	              (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   458	            (ldPointCLLinear P
   459	                (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   460	                (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
   461	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   462	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   463	            (chiIndex P
   464	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   465	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   466	          (ldPointCLLinear P
   467	              (LdSpace.direction
   468	                (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   469	                  (chiIndex P
   470	                    (LdSpace.seed
   471	                      (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   472	                  (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
   473	              (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
   474	    rw [hseed, hdir]
   475	  rw [hval]
   476	  funext i
   477	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   478	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
   479	        (lineRepMap
   480	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   481	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
   482	      lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   483	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   484	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   485	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   486	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   487	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   488	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   489	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   490	            (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
   491	          ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
   492	      prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
   493	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]

    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on

    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.

    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is

    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q

    48	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    49	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    50	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    51	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    54	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    55	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin

    58	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=

    61	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed

    63	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    65	-/
    66	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    67	
    68	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    93	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    94	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))

    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=

   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=

   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface

   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   157	-/
   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j

   205	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :

   208	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   209	    (fun s =>
