   212	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   217	-/
   218	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   219	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   220	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   221	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl

   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩

   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end

    32	/-!
    33	### Formalization-only auxiliary facts on finite distributions
    34	
    35	The statements of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
    36	elementary behaviour of push-forwards of uniform distributions that the proofs
    37	of `lem:alnf`, `lem:dlnf`, and of the identification of the low-degree sampler
    38	with a typed conditionally linear distribution rely on.

    40	
    41	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: two finite distributions coincide as
    42	soon as their supports and their weight functions coincide. -/
    43	private theorem distribution_ext {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
    44	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) : μ = ν := by
    45	  cases μ with
    46	  | mk s w hn ho =>
    47	    cases ν with
    48	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
    49	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
    50	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
    51	      subst hs
    52	      subst hw
    53	      rfl
    54	
    55	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: successive push-forwards compose. -/
    56	private theorem distribution_map_map {α β γ : Type*}
    57	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    58	    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
    59	    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
    60	  refine distribution_ext ?_ ?_
    61	  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
    62	    rw [Finset.image_image]
    63	    rfl
    64	  · funext c
    65	    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
    66	        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
    67	      intro a ha
    68	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
    69	      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
    70	    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
    71	    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
    72	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
    73	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
    74	    rw [← hkey]
    75	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
    76	    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
    77	    congr 1
    78	    ext a
    79	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    80	    constructor
    81	    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
    82	      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
    83	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
    84	      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩
    85

    32	/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
    33	descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
    34	the same effect as applying it once. -/
    35	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    36	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    37	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    38	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]

    40	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    41	inductive LineKind where
    42	  | axis
    43	  | diagonal
    44	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    45	
    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    47	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :

   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, blueprint
   111	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-48`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none

   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point

   414	/-- The uniform distribution on a specified finite support.
   415	
   416	The stored support is `s`, and the weight of a point is the elementary finite
   417	uniform weight `1 / s.card` on `s` and `0` off `s`.  When the support is empty
   418	this gives the zero sub-probability distribution, matching the convention used
   419	for degenerate filtered supports in the LDT development. -/
   420	noncomputable def uniformOnFinset {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) : Distribution α :=
   421	  letI := Classical.decEq α
   422	  { support := s
   423	    weight := fun a => if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0
   424	    nonnegative := fun _ => by
   425	      split_ifs <;> positivity
   426	    outsideSupport := fun _ ha => by
   427	      simp [ha] }
   428	
   429	@[simp]
   430	theorem uniformOnFinset_support {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) :
   431	    (uniformOnFinset s).support = s := rfl
   432	
   433	@[simp]
   434	theorem uniformOnFinset_weight {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (s : Finset α) (a : α) :
   435	    (uniformOnFinset s).weight a =
   436	      if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0 := by
   437	  by_cases ha : a ∈ s
   438	  · simp [uniformOnFinset, ha]
   439	  · simp [uniformOnFinset, ha]
   440	
   441	/-- A nonempty finite support gives a probability distribution. -/
   442	theorem uniformOnFinset_isProbability {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
   443	    (uniformOnFinset s).IsProbability := by
   444	  classical
   445	  dsimp [IsProbability, totalWeight]
   446	  simp_rw [uniformOnFinset_weight]
   447	  have hcard_nat : s.card ≠ 0 := Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr hs
   448	  have hcard : (s.card : Error) ≠ 0 := by
   449	    exact_mod_cast hcard_nat
   450	  have hsum :
   451	      (∑ a ∈ s, if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0) =
   452	        ∑ _a ∈ s, 1 / (s.card : Error) := by
   453	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   454	    intro a ha
   455	    simp [ha]
   456	  rw [hsum]
   457	  simp [Finset.sum_const, hcard]
   458	
   459	/-- The uniform distribution on any finite support is a sub-probability
   460	distribution.  It has mass `1` on nonempty support and mass `0` on empty
   461	support. -/
   462	theorem uniformOnFinset_weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) :
   463	    ∑ a ∈ (uniformOnFinset s).support, (uniformOnFinset s).weight a ≤ 1 := by
   464	  classical
   465	  by_cases hs : s.Nonempty
   466	  · exact (uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs).weight_sum_le_one
   467	  · have hsempty : s = ∅ := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hs
   468	    simp [hsempty]

   470	/-- The project uniform distribution on a nonempty finite support is Mathlib's
   471	uniform probability mass function on that support. -/
   472	theorem uniformOnFinset_toPMF
   473	    {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
   474	    (uniformOnFinset s).toPMF (uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs) =
   475	      PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs := by
   476	  ext a
   477	  rw [toPMF_apply]
   478	  rw [show (uniformOnFinset s).weight a =
   479	      (PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs a).toReal by
   480	        classical
   481	        by_cases ha : a ∈ s
   482	        · simp [uniformOnFinset_weight, PMF.uniformOfFinset_apply, ha,
   483	            ENNReal.toReal_inv, ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
   484	        · simp [uniformOnFinset_weight, PMF.uniformOfFinset_apply, ha]]
   485	  exact ENNReal.ofReal_toReal ((PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs).apply_ne_top a)

   501	theorem uniformDistribution_weight_sum_eq_one (α : Type*)
   502	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :

   512	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}

+### Formalization-only auxiliary facts on finite distributions
+
+The statements of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
+elementary behaviour of push-forwards of uniform distributions that the proofs
+of `lem:alnf`, `lem:dlnf`, and of the identification of the low-degree sampler
+with a typed conditionally linear distribution rely on.

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: two finite distributions coincide as
+soon as their supports and their weight functions coincide. -/
+private theorem distribution_ext {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) : μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: successive push-forwards compose. -/
+private theorem distribution_map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
+    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
+  refine distribution_ext ?_ ?_
+  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
+    rw [Finset.image_image]
+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
+        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
+      intro a ha
+      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
+    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
+    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
+        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
+      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
+    rw [← hkey]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
+    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    congr 1
+    ext a
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
+      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every point of a finite type carries
+the same uniform weight. -/
+private theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
+  simp [uniformDistribution]

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: a map whose fibers all have the same
+cardinality pushes the uniform distribution forward to the uniform
+distribution. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
+    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
+    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
+  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
+    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
+    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
+      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
+    rwa [hc] at hpos
+  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
+    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
+      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
+      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
+    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
+    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
+    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
+  refine distribution_ext ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
+    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
+      exact hcpos
+    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
+    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩

+    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
+    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'

+        (uniformDistribution α).weight a) = (uniformDistribution β).weight b

+      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Finset.sum_const, hc, nsmul_eq_mul, hcard]
+    push_cast
+    field_simp

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: relabelling along a bijection preserves
+uniformity. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_equiv {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map E = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine map_uniformDistribution_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => E a = b) = {E.symm b} := by
+    ext a
+    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
+  rw [hfilter]
+  simp

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the first marginal of the uniform
+distribution on a product is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_fst {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by
+  refine map_uniformDistribution_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_

+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton, and_true]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the second marginal of the uniform
+distribution on a product is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_snd {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by

+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: binding a uniform type distribution to a

+distribution on the product. -/
+private theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (g : α → β → γ) :

+      simp only [Finset.card_filter]

+### Formalization-only auxiliary facts about the ambient low-degree space
+-/

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
+vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
+private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
+    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
+  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
+  invFun p := fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
+    | .inr j => p.2 j
+  left_inv z := by
+    funext i
+    rcases i with (j | u) | j
+    · rfl
+    · cases u
+      rfl
+    · rfl
+  right_inv p := by
+    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
+    rfl
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random
+ambient vector is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
+      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
+  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
+      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+    map_uniformDistribution_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
+  calc
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
+        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [distribution_map_map, distribution_map_map]
+          rfl
+    _ = ((uniformDistribution
+          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
+    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [map_uniformDistribution_fst]
+    _ = uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := map_uniformDistribution_fst
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared scalar coordinate of a
+uniformly random ambient vector is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_seed (L : LdParams) :
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed =
+      uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L) := by
+  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
+      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+    map_uniformDistribution_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
+  calc
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed
+        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.snd := by
+          rw [distribution_map_map, distribution_map_map]
+          rfl
+    _ = ((uniformDistribution
+          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.snd := by rw [hsplit]
+    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.snd := by
+          rw [map_uniformDistribution_fst]
+    _ = uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L) := map_uniformDistribution_snd

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: an admissible field size is positive. -/
+private theorem ldParams_q_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q := by
+  obtain ⟨j, -, hj⟩ := L.hq
+  rw [hj]
+  exact Nat.pow_pos (by norm_num)

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the coordinate index of a scalar is
+read off from its binary representation. -/
+private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
+    chiIndex L s = i ↔
+      ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val := by
+  rw [Fin.ext_iff]
+  simp [chiIndex]

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
+exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
+`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
+private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
+    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
+      = L.q / L.m := by
+  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
+  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
+  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
+    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
+      omega
+    · exact h
+  have hstep1 :
+      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
+        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
+            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
+    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
+  have hstep2 :
+      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
+        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
+            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
+    ext t
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
+      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
+      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
+  have hstep3 :
+      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
+        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
+    ext t
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
+      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
+        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
+        omega
+      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
+        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
+      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
+      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
+        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
+        omega
+      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
+          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
+      rw [hdiv] at hle
+      omega
+    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
+      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
+          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
+      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
+        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
+        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
+          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
+          omega
+        omega
+      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
+      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
+          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
+        omega
+      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
+  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
+      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter

+    (k : Fin ell) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
+    d.marginal k x a = 0 := by
+  rw [d.sum_formula, Finset.sum_apply]
+  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+  intro i _
+  split_ifs
+  · exact d.linear_supported i _ _ a (fun hai => ha (d.factor_subset i _ hai))
+  · rfl
+
+/-- Every strict-prefix marginal in support-relative decomposition data is
+supported on the active register. -/
+private theorem CLDataOn.prefix_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (d : CLDataOn K ι S ell L)
+    (k : Fin ell) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
+    clPrefix d.marginal k x a = 0 := by
+  unfold clPrefix
+  split_ifs
+  · rfl
+  · exact d.marginal_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ x ha
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zero {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x = 0 := by
+  cases t
+  rfl
+
+/-- A one-level representation of a conditionally linear function has
+support-relative prefix decomposition data. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 1)
+    {S : Finset ι} (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
+    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S 1 (CondLinearTerm.eval t)) := by
+  cases t with
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
+      refine ⟨{
+        marginal := fun _ => CondLinearTerm.eval (.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest)
+        factor := fun _ _ => S
+        linear := fun _ _ => L₁.comp (coordinateRestrictionLinear S₁)
+        marginal_cl := ?_
+        factor_subset := ?_
+        factor_disjoint := ?_
+        factor_cover := ?_
+        linear_supported := ?_
+        sum_formula := ?_
+        top := ?_
+      }⟩
+      · intro k
+        have hk : k = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
+        subst k
+        exact ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest, ht, rfl⟩
+      · intro k u
+        exact Finset.Subset.rfl
+      · intro x i j hij
+        exact (hij (Subsingleton.elim i j)).elim
+      · intro x a ha
+        exact ⟨0, ha⟩
+      · intro k u x a ha
+        change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) a = 0
+        exact hSupport _ _ (fun haS₁ => ha (ht.1 haS₁))
+      · intro k x
+        have hk : k = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
+        subst k
+        simp only [Fin.sum_univ_one, Fin.isValue, le_refl, ↓reduceIte]
+        change CondLinearTerm.eval (.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest) x =
+          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (coordinateRestriction S x))
+        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction ht.1]
+        change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
+            CondLinearTerm.eval
+              (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _
+        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_zero]
+        exact add_zero _
+      · intro h
+        rfl
+
+/-- The first linear contribution in the inductive prefix decomposition. -/
+private def clDataFirst {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
+  L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)
+
+/-- Add the first contribution to each marginal of residual decomposition
+data. -/
+private def clDataConsMarginal {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) :
+    Fin (ell + 1) → (ι → K) → (ι → K) :=
+  Fin.cases (clDataFirst S₁ L₁) fun k x =>
+    clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x + (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x
+
+/-- Select the first or residual factor register from a combined prefix. -/
+private def clDataConsFactor {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) :
+    Fin (ell + 1) → (ι → K) → Finset ι :=
+  Fin.cases (fun _ => S₁) fun k u =>
+    (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).factor k (coordinateRestriction T u)
+
+/-- Select the first or residual linear map from a combined prefix. -/
+private def clDataConsLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) :
+    Fin (ell + 1) → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K)) :=
+  Fin.cases (fun _ => L₁.comp (coordinateRestrictionLinear S₁)) fun k u =>
+    (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).linear k (coordinateRestriction T u)
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsMarginal_zero {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) (x : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d 0 x = clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x := rfl
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsMarginal_succ {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) (k : Fin ell) (x : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d k.succ x =
+      clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x +
+        (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x := rfl
+
+private theorem clPrefix_cons_succ {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y)) (k : Fin (ell + 1))
+    (x : ι → K) :
+    clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) k.succ x =
+      clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x +
+        clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x := by
+  cases k using Fin.cases with
+  | zero => simp [clPrefix]
+  | succ k =>
+      simp only [clPrefix]
+      change clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d (Fin.castSucc k).succ x =
+        clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x +
+          (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal (Fin.castSucc k) x
+      rfl
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsFactor_zero {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) (u : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsFactor S₁ d 0 u = S₁ := rfl
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsFactor_succ {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y))
+    (k : Fin ell) (u : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsFactor S₁ d k.succ u =
+      (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).factor k (coordinateRestriction T u) := rfl
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsLinear_zero {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) (u : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d 0 u =
+      L₁.comp (coordinateRestrictionLinear S₁) := rfl
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem clDataConsLinear_succ {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T ell (R y)) (k : Fin ell) (u : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d k.succ u =
+      (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).linear k (coordinateRestriction T u) := rfl
+
+private theorem coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_left
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y))
+    (hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ T) (k : Fin (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
+    coordinateRestriction S₁
+        (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) k.succ x) =
+      clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x := by
+  rw [clPrefix_cons_succ, coordinateRestriction_add]
+  have hfirst : coordinateRestriction S₁ (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x) =
+      clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x :=
+    coordinateRestriction_eq_self (x := clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x) (hSupport _)
+  have htail : coordinateRestriction S₁
+      (clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x) = 0 :=
+    coordinateRestriction_eq_zero_of_disjoint hDisjoint
+      (fun a ha =>
+        (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).prefix_eq_zero_of_not_mem k x ha)
+  rw [hfirst, htail]
+  exact add_zero _
+
+private theorem coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_right
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y))
+    (hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ T) (k : Fin (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
+    coordinateRestriction T
+        (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) k.succ x) =
+      clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x := by
+  rw [clPrefix_cons_succ, coordinateRestriction_add]
+  have hfirst : coordinateRestriction T (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x) = 0 :=
+    coordinateRestriction_eq_zero_of_disjoint hDisjoint.symm (hSupport _)
+  have htail : coordinateRestriction T
+      (clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x) =
+        clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x :=
+    coordinateRestriction_eq_self
+      (fun a ha =>
+        (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).prefix_eq_zero_of_not_mem k x ha)
+  rw [hfirst, htail]
+  exact zero_add _
+
+private theorem clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y))
+    (hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ T) (k : Fin (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsFactor S₁ d k.succ
+        (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) k.succ x) =
+      (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor k
+        (clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x) := by
+  rw [clDataConsFactor_succ]
+  rw [coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_left S₁ L₁ hSupport d
+    hDisjoint]
+  rw [coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_right S₁ L₁ hSupport d
+    hDisjoint]
+
+private theorem clDataConsLinear_prefix_succ
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {T : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
+    {R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K)}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y))
+    (hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ T) (k : Fin (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
+    clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d k.succ
+        (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) k.succ x) =
+      (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).linear k
+        (clPrefix (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal k x) := by
+  rw [clDataConsLinear_succ]
+  rw [coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_left S₁ L₁ hSupport d
+    hDisjoint]
+  rw [coordinateRestriction_clPrefix_cons_succ_right S₁ L₁ hSupport d
+    hDisjoint]
+
+/-- Prepending a syntax stage to support-relative residual data produces
+support-relative data at the next level. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_succ
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    (S₁ : Finset ι) (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1))
+    {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest) S)
+    (hd : ∀ y, Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι (S \ S₁) (ell + 1)
+      (fun x => CondLinearTerm.eval (rest y) x))) :
+    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S ((ell + 1) + 1)
+      (CondLinearTerm.eval (.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest))) := by
+  classical
+  let d := fun y => Classical.choice (hd y)
+  have hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ (S \ S₁) := Finset.disjoint_sdiff
+  refine ⟨{
+    marginal := clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d
+    factor := clDataConsFactor S₁ d
+    linear := clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d
+    marginal_cl := ?_
+    factor_subset := ?_
+    factor_disjoint := ?_
+    factor_cover := ?_
+    linear_supported := ?_
+    sum_formula := ?_
+    top := ?_
+  }⟩
+  · intro k
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) k
+    · refine ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport (fun _ => .zero), ⟨ht.1, fun _ => trivial⟩, ?_⟩
+      funext x
+      simp [CondLinearTerm.eval, clDataFirst]
+    · rw [show clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d i.succ =
+          (fun x => clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x +
+            (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).marginal i x) by
+          funext x
+          rfl]
+      simpa only [clDataFirst, Fin.val_succ, Nat.add_assoc] using
+        (IsCondLinearOn.cons L₁ ht.1 hSupport
+          (fun y x => (d y).marginal i x) (fun y => (d y).marginal_cl i))
+  · intro k u
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) k
+    · exact ht.1
+    · exact ((d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).factor_subset i _).trans
+          Finset.sdiff_subset
+  · intro x i j hij
+    cases i using Fin.cases with
+    | zero =>
+        cases j using Fin.cases with
+        | zero => exact (hij rfl).elim
+        | succ j =>
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_zero]
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            exact hDisjoint.mono_right
+              ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_subset j _)
+    | succ i =>
+        cases j using Fin.cases with
+        | zero =>
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_zero]
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            exact (hDisjoint.mono_right
+              ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_subset i _)).symm
+        | succ j =>
+            have hij' : i ≠ j := by
+              intro h
+              subst j
+              exact hij rfl
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            exact (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_disjoint x i j hij'
+  · intro x a ha
+    by_cases haS₁ : a ∈ S₁
+    · exact ⟨0, by simpa using haS₁⟩
+    · have haTail : a ∈ S \ S₁ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨ha, haS₁⟩
+      obtain ⟨i, hai⟩ :=
+        (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_cover x a haTail
+      refine ⟨i.succ, ?_⟩
+      rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+      exact hai
+  · intro k u x a ha
+    revert ha
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) k
+    · intro ha
+      change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) a = 0
+      exact hSupport _ _ ha
+    · intro ha
+      exact (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).linear_supported i
+          (coordinateRestriction (S \ S₁) u) x a ha
+  · intro k x
+    have hhead :
+        clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d 0
+            (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) 0 x)
+            (coordinateRestriction
+              (clDataConsFactor S₁ d 0
+                (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) 0 x)) x) =
+          clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x := by
+      change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) =
+        L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)
+      rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.Subset.rfl]
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun j => ?_) k
+    · rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
+      simp only [Fin.val_zero, le_refl, ↓reduceIte, hhead]
+      simp
+    · rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
+      simp only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.zero_le, ↓reduceIte, hhead]
+      rw [clDataConsMarginal_succ]
+      congr 1
+      rw [(d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).sum_formula j x]
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro i _
+      by_cases hij : i.val ≤ j.val
+      · have hsucc : i.succ.val ≤ j.succ.val := by
+          simpa only [Fin.val_succ, Nat.succ_le_succ_iff] using hij
+        rw [if_pos hsucc, if_pos hij]
+        rw [clDataConsLinear_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+        rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+      · have hsucc : ¬ i.succ.val ≤ j.succ.val := by
+          simpa only [Fin.val_succ, Nat.succ_le_succ_iff] using hij
+        rw [if_neg hsucc, if_neg hij]
+  · intro h
+    have hTail : 0 < ell + 1 := by omega
+    let last : Fin (ell + 1) :=
+      ⟨(ell + 1) - 1, Nat.sub_lt hTail (by decide)⟩
+    have hlast :
+        (⟨((ell + 1) + 1) - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ : Fin ((ell + 1) + 1)) =
+          last.succ := by
+      apply Fin.ext
+      simp [last]
+    funext x
+    rw [hlast, clDataConsMarginal_succ]
+    rw [congrFun ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).top hTail) x]
+    rfl
+
+/-- Every positive-level supported representation of a conditionally linear
+function admits support-relative prefix decomposition data. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
+    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
+    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S ell (CondLinearTerm.eval t)) := by
+  induction ell using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing S with
+  | h ell ih =>
+      cases ell with
+      | zero => omega
+      | succ n =>
+          cases n with
+          | zero => exact CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one t ht
+          | succ n =>
+              cases t with
+              | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
+                  apply CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ht
+                  intro y
+                  exact ih (n + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (rest y) (ht.2 y)
+
 /-- A map is `ell`-level conditionally linear exactly when it admits the
 prefix decomposition of `lem:cl-kth`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`,
 paper `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-262`. -/
 theorem isCondLinear_iff_nonempty_clData {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
     [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
     (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
     IsCondLinear ell L ↔ Nonempty (CLData K ι ell L) := by
-  sorry
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
+    rw [← ht_eval]

     1	\chapter{The Pauli basis test}
     2	\label{chap:qpbt-test}
     3	% Paper label sec:pauli-verifier kept for cross-reference fidelity; it resolves to this chapter.
     4	\label{sec:pauli-verifier}
     5	
     6	This chapter defines the two testing primitives underlying the question-reduction step: the \emph{classical low individual degree game}, in its simultaneous form, and the \emph{Pauli basis test}, a nonlocal game built from the classical game together with the Magic Square game. We state the quantum soundness of the classical game (Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, imported, with the facts required by the identification, which remain to be proved, recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; see Remark~\ref{rem:ld-soundness-provider}), the rigidity of the Magic Square game (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}, imported), completeness of the Pauli basis test (Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}), and the main soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test (Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}), whose proof occupies Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}--\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} and is completed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} only modulo the proof obligation documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. The chapter closes with the qubit form of the soundness statement (Corollary~\ref{cor:pauli-binary}) and the canonical parameter choice with its soundness bound (Definition~\ref{def:introparams}, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta-bound}).
     7	
     8	Throughout, the two players are denoted $\mathrm A$ and $\mathrm B$; for $w \in \{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$ we write $\overline w$ for the other player. Games, strategies, values, conditionally linear (CL) functions and distributions, typed distributions sampled from the edges of a graph, and the state-dependent approximation $\approx_\delta$ between families of measurement operators are as in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-games}; the algebraic material on lines, canonical linear maps, the low-degree encoding, and generalized Pauli observables is from Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}.

    10	\section{The classical low individual degree game}
    11	% Paper labels sec:ld-verifier and sec:ld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
    12	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    13	\label{sec:ld-game}
    14	
    15	The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.
    16	
    17	\begin{definition}[The classical low individual degree game: parameters and registers]\label{def:ld-game}
    18		\uses{def:game, def:admissible-size}
    19		% The source fixes \N to be the set of positive integers
    20		% (references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:6) and takes m, d, ldc in \N
    21		% (references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:33-35),
    22		% so the positivity below is the source's implicit domain, stated explicitly.
    23		% It is load-bearing: at d = 0 or k = 0 the prefactor a(dmk)^a of delta_ld in
    24		% lem:ld-soundness vanishes, and at d = 0 the resulting exact conclusions fail
    25		% (e.g. at (q,m,d,k) = (2,1,0,1) with eps = 1). The case k = 0, though it would
    26		% hold trivially, is likewise outside the source's domain and is omitted.
    27		The game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ is parametrized by a tuple $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$, where $m, d, k \ge 1$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}), and $m$ divides $q$. We write $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$ to emphasize the dependence on the parameter tuple. The type set of $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ is
    28		\[
    29			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} = \{\mathsf{Point}, \mathsf{ALine}, \mathsf{DLine}\}\;,
    30		\]
    31		and the distribution over type pairs $(t_{\mathrm A}, t_{\mathrm B})$ is uniform over $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} \times \mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}}$. The ambient space is the direct sum $V = V_X \oplus V_I \oplus V_V$ of three register subspaces: the \emph{point register} $V_X \cong \F_q^m$, the \emph{coordinate register} $V_I \cong \F_q$, and the \emph{direction register} $V_V \cong \F_q^m$. Elements of $V$ are identified with triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$. The question distribution and the win predicate of $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ are specified in Definitions~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} and~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} below.
    32	\end{definition}
    33	
    34	\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the classical low individual degree game]\label{def:ld-question-distribution}
    35		\uses{def:ld-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, lem:cl-concat, def:cl-canonical, def:line-representative}
    36		Let $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}. Define $L_{\mathsf{Point}}$ to be the $1$-level CL function on $V$ that projects onto $V_X$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
    37		\begin{equation}
    38			\label{eq:cl-ptf}
    39			L_{\mathsf{Point}}(u,s,v) = (u,0,0)\;.
    40		\end{equation}
    41		For $s \in \F_q$, let $\chi(s)$ be the unique integer such that
    42		\begin{equation}
    43			\label{eq:chi-func}
    44			s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m} + r
    45		\end{equation}
    46		for some $0 \le r < q/m$, where $s$ is interpreted as an integer in $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$ under the identification of $\F_q$ with binary strings fixed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}. Since $m$ divides $q$, when $s$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q$ the index $\chi(s)$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$. Define $L_{\mathsf{ALine}}$ by
    47		\begin{equation}
    48			\label{eq:cl-alnf}
    49			L_{\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\, s,\, 0\bigr)\quad\text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V\;,
    50		\end{equation}
    51		where $i = \chi(s)$ and $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ denotes the canonical linear map with one-dimensional kernel spanned by $v$, used to compute canonical representatives of lines (Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}). The function $L_{\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the concatenation (in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-concat}) of the $1$-level CL function projecting $V_I \oplus V_V$ onto $V_I$ with the family of $1$-level CL functions $\{L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}\}$ on $V_X$ indexed by $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$; thus $L_{\mathsf{ALine}}$ is a $2$-level CL function. Define $L_{\mathsf{DLine}}$ by
    52		\begin{equation}
    53			\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
    54			L_{\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\, s,\, \pi_{i-1}(v)\bigr)\;,
    55		\end{equation}

+The statements of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: two finite distributions coincide as

+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
+vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
+private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
+    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
+  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
+  invFun p := fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
+    | .inr j => p.2 j
+  left_inv z := by
+    funext i
+    rcases i with (j | u) | j
+    · rfl
+    · cases u
+      rfl
+    · rfl
+  right_inv p := by
+    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
+    rfl

+    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [map_uniformDistribution_fst]

+        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter

+    ext t

+      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]

+    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩

+      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)

   635	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   636	  classical
   637	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   638	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   639	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   640	  funext x
   641	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   642	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   643	  intro j _
   644	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   645	
   646	/--
   647	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   648	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   649	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   650	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   651	-/
   652	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   653	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   654	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   655	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   656	
   657	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   658	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   659	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   660	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   661	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   662	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   663	-/
   664	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   665	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   666	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   667	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   668	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   669	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   670	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   671	
   672	/--
   673	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   674	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:548-559`, with
   675	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   676	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   677	-/
   678	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   679	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   680	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   681	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   682	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   683	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   684	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   685	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   686	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   687	  classical
   688	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   689	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   690	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   691	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   692	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   693	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   694	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   695	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   696	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   697	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   698	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   699	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   700	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   701	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   702	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   703	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   704	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   705	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   706	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   707	    have huniv :
   708	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   709	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   710	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   711	      ext i
   712	      cases i <;> simp
   713	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   714	  · funext x
   715	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   716	    simp only [zero_add]
   717	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   718	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   719	    rfl
   720	
   721	/--
   722	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   723	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   724	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:679-691`;
   725	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   726	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   727	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   728	-/
   729	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   730	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   731	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   732	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   733	
   734	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   735	nonempty.  This is `lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   736	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:693-698`. -/
   737	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   738	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   739	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   740	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   741	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   742	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   743	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   744	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   745	
   746	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   210	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))

   656	private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]

   661	  induction ell using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing S with

   664	      | zero => omega
   665	      | succ n =>
   666	          cases n with
   667	          | zero => exact CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one t ht

   675	/-- A map is `ell`-level conditionally linear exactly when it admits the
   676	prefix decomposition of `lem:cl-kth`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`,
   677	paper `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-262`. -/
   678	theorem isCondLinear_iff_nonempty_clData {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   679	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
   680	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   681	    IsCondLinear ell L ↔ Nonempty (CLData K ι ell L) := by
   682	  constructor
   683	  · rintro ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
   684	    rw [← ht_eval]
   685	    obtain ⟨d⟩ := CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn hEll t ht
   686	    exact ⟨{
   687	      marginal := d.marginal
   688	      factor := d.factor
   689	      linear := d.linear
   690	      marginal_cl := d.marginal_cl
   691	      factor_disjoint := d.factor_disjoint
   692	      factor_cover := fun x a => d.factor_cover x a (Finset.mem_univ a)
   693	      linear_supported := d.linear_supported
   694	      sum_formula := d.sum_formula
   695	      top := d.top
   696	    }⟩
   697	  · rintro ⟨d⟩
   698	    have hPos : 0 < ell := by omega
   699	    let last : Fin ell := ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt hPos (by decide)⟩
   700	    have hLast := d.marginal_cl last
   701	    rw [d.top hPos] at hLast
   702	    simpa only [IsCondLinear, last, Nat.sub_add_cancel hEll] using hLast
   703	
   704	/-- Coordinate direct sum of maps supported on a finite register partition.
   705	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   706	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:565-576`, paper
   707	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
   708	def condLinearDirectSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ}
   709	    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   710	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
   711	  ∑ j : Fin m, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   712	
   713	/-- Maximum of the levels in a finite direct sum. This formalization-only
   714	auxiliary uses `0` for the empty family; `lem:cl-func-prod` separately assumes
   715	the source boundary `m ≥ 1`. -/
   716	def directSumLevel {m : ℕ} (ell : Fin m → ℕ) : ℕ :=
   717	  Finset.univ.sup ell
   718	
   719	/-- Direct sums over a register partition preserve conditional linearity. The
   720	level-zero case is included explicitly, as required by the local correction to
   721	`lem:cl-func-prod`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:565-576`, paper
   722	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
   723	theorem IsCondLinear.directSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   724	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
   725	    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
   726	    (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   727	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   728	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)

    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and

   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}

   288	  \begin{equation*}
